title: Personalized benefit information changes the choice between Social Security Disability and early retirement applications
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35748 using Social Security statements and application behavior among older U.S. adults
geography: United States; people ages 62 to full retirement age, with work-limiting health conditions or low work ability

observations.period: Social Security statement and benefit-application period; paper issued September 14, 2026

denominator.unit: U.S. people ages 62 to full retirement age in the study data; exact abstract denominator not disclosed

information_treatment.value: initial Social Security statement with personalized estimated DI and OAI benefit amounts

application_response.value: increased probability of applying for both programs
application_response.unit: application behavior among people with a work-limiting health condition or low work ability

di_application_composition.value: increase split between DI-only applications and applications for both DI and OAI

age_gradient.value: response concentrated among people further from full retirement age
age_gradient.unit: heterogeneity by distance from full retirement age

award_boundary.value: application response, not verified award or benefit receipt

observations.method: Examines the effect of receiving an initial Social Security statement containing personalized estimated DI and OAI benefit amounts on applications for Disability Insurance and Old-Age Insurance among people ages 62 to full retirement age, with subgroup analysis by health/work ability and distance from full retirement age.
observations.uncertainty: The paper is a working paper and the abstract does not disclose the exact denominator, statement-delivery process, or award and appeals outcomes. Application is not approval, receipt, income adequacy, health improvement, reduced work burden, or household security.
observations.subgroup: People ages 62 to full retirement age with a work-limiting health condition or low work ability, applicants for DI only, OAI only, or both, and people at different distances from full retirement age.
observations.counterinterpretation: Personalized statements may change awareness or timing without changing ultimate eligibility or benefit receipt. People further from full retirement age may have different health, labor-market, wealth, or information constraints; increased applications could increase administrative burden if awards do not rise.

related_sources.claim: Official NBER DOI identifies the working paper.

boundary: This record establishes an information-interface-to-benefit-application pathway for older U.S. adults with health or work limitations. It does not establish awards, receipt, benefit adequacy, health, work exit, household security, trust, or administrative cost.
